ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Arts. L. 561-1 et seq. and R. 561-1 et seq.; Loi n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Sapin II); Code de commerce, Arts. L. 123-123 and R. 123-220 to R. 123-229-3; Règlements (UE) 2015/849, 2018/843 and 2023/1113; Décret n° 2020-118 on the national UBO register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration (extrait K-bis or equivalent) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) or Consular Legalization if country is not party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney to the French incorporation agent for signature of the articles of association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary in the shareholder jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national ID of each individual UBO and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary or authorized public certifying officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization on the notarial certification of signature

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and commercial counterparties against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, French Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) asset-freezing measures, OFAC SDN List, and TRACFIN/e-Ficoba. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons under FATF Recommendation 12 and EU Directive 2015/849. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification for ISIC 4651 (wholesale of SSDs and server CPUs), transaction monitoring, source-of-funds documentation and UBO attestation are obligatory prior to incorporation and for each Escrow_Inspection_Wire transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with official company-record search via the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) using data.inpi.fr and Infogreffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is mandatory under Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Loi Toubon) and Article L. 123-1 of the Code de commerce. The corporate name must be expressed in Latin script, must not create confusion with existing RCS names, and may contain a foreign term only if accompanied by a French translation or where the term is commonly recognized. Non-Latin names must be transliterated into French and the transliteration must be certified by a sworn translator.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the INPI/guichet unique emits a reasoned non-regularisation notice. The founder may re-file the same form with a corrected name or attachments using the same portal; any statutory period not yet lapsed is paused. For a formal appeal against a registry refusal, the applicant must file a requête in référé before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of the refusal, relying on Articles L. 123-1 and R. 123-31 et seq. of the Code de commerce. Where rejection is based on infringement of a prior trademark, the applicant may also file observations with INPI or, where necessary, a nullity/infringement action before the Paris Judicial Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted for the SAS commercial domiciliation if the provider is licensed by the local préfecture and provides a physical mailing address, document retention, and a meeting room on request. For ISIC 4651 (spot semiconductor trading), a purely administrative address without any operational substance would not satisfy French tax residence or VAT fixed-establishment doctrine; a commercial complement such as a warehousing or inspection point in France is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high risk quantified at 35-45% during the first two operating years, attributable to unannounced tax audits, DGDDI customs inspections, and labour inspector visits; the high unit value and cross-border wire profile of SSD/CPU wholesale materially increases on-site substance verification likelihood.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS); Implementing Decree No. 2017-921.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, receiving filings through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (standard registration form for creating a legal entity) accompanied by the signed Articles of Association (statuts).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: French law imposes no minimum issued share capital for an SAS; the Articles fix the amount. Cash contributions must be blocked in escrow and evidenced by the bank's attestation de blocage, while in-kind contributions must be fully paid and supported by a commissaire aux apports report. Shares may be split into par-value units; liberalisation of ordinary shares may be deferred, but all restrictive issuance requirements of the Articles must be met.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Shareholders of the SAS adopted in a single deliberation the following resolutions: (i) each resolution confirms the subscription and full allocation of the share capital at EUR [   ], composed of [   ] shares of EUR [  ] each to the persons named on the subscription form; (ii) the final Articles are approved as read; (iii) the registered office is hereby fixed at [    ], France; (iv) [Name Surname] is appointed Président of the Société, with authority to represent the company in dealings with third parties, to sign for the company, and to execute all legal, tax, and banking formalities; (v) [Name Surname] is appointed Directeur Général, if any; (vi) the Président is authorized to publish notices, register the company and apply for any permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company legal counsel or optional notaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language Articles of Association in statutory form, including corporate purpose limited to ISIC 4651, share capital, registered office, the President's corporate governance powers, and procedures for collective decisions. Circulate final statutory text to shareholders and obtain identically executed signature pages; obtain a commissaire aux comptes or commissaire aux apports report if any in-kind contribution is made.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts in French
List of shareholders with subscription amounts
In-kind contribution report, if applicable
Identity documents of shareholders and intended President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries statutory defects, cure by amending the Articles and having all shareholders re-execute the corrected pages before submitting the new version through the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocked funds attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French retail bank or other lawful financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the future company's name, receive cash contributions from shareholders, and block the funds until the registration certificate is received. Request an attestation de blocage des fonds from the bank. If in-kind contributions are used, ensure the value was audited and the contribution deed is executed.
required_dossiers: Corporate name and proof of identity
Provisional certified copy of the Articles
Government-issued ID of account applicant
Deed of contribution for in-kind assets, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the capital attestation, obtain from a notaire a certificate of funds received or correct the legal deficiency in the opening mandate and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish the incorporation notice in a local legal gazette. The notice must include the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and identity of the first President. Retain the printed publication certificate.
required_dossiers: Notice text signed by the President-designate
Articles of Association draft
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is defective for reasons such as an incompatible legal object or incomplete capital declaration, republish a corrected notice within 8 days and annex the correction to the main registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, operated by INPI via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 incorporation form online, attach the executed Articles, bank capital attestation, publication certificate, and director identities; submit the package through the platform. Track receipt notifications and set the intended registration date.
required_dossiers: Formulaire M0 duly signed
Articles of Association in French
Attestation de blocage des fonds
JAL publication certificate
Statement of no prior RCS registration and no criminal convictions for the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Uniqu identifies missing or inconsistent documents, correct the file electronically within the proposed deadline. A failure to act before the closing date causes a rejection that can be cured by filing a fully new dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry control and issuance of Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The greffe verifies legality, confers the RCS number, and registrants the company in the SIRENE directory. Upon completion, the greffe issues the official Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers.
required_dossiers: Receipt of the Guichet Unique transmission
Identity proof of the President and any delegated director
Declaration of beneficial owner for the annual BODACC
Attestation proving business premises comply with general administrative requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe rejects the application, respond through the Guichet Unique within the statutory refusal period or request rectification. Judicial appeals are brought before the tribunal de commerce, usually with the assistance of counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation for tax, social security and statistical purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, INSEE, and the competent tax office (DGFIP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Kbis, file the creation with URSSAF and the tax administration, select corporate income tax (IS) or the applicable default, register for VAT, and request the relevant APE/NAF code corresponding to ISIC 4651. Confirm the registration in the professional and tax files.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Banking details (RIB)
Tax form for creation of a company
Registered office lease or proof of ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or URSSAF activation delays beyond the service level, file a correction request on the relevant online portal and send a signed letter by recorded delivery to the competent local unit to force processing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and the local Préfecture, acting under the Ministry for Ecological Transition.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Declaration or authorization for stored warehouse and logistical site under ICPE procedure, Rubric 1510 of the French Environmental Code, together with any local town planning permit (certificat d'urbanisme, permis de construire or modification) if the building footprint changes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 (Déclaration) if the warehouse storage volume is below 1000 tonnes and the site is not in a sensitive zone; a full EIA is not required for low-throughput wholesale premises. If the storage volume exceeds 1000 tonnes or the site is in a protected area, a full environmental impact register or an actual EIA report may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater and non-process water discharges must meet local municipal sewer by-laws and the concentration thresholds of Article R.1331-2 of the French Public Health Code. No significant VOCs are expected from storage of SSD and CPU chips, but any refrigeration or inert gas discharge must respect the relevant Code de l'environnement gas dispersion limits. Waste electrical and electronic equipment must be handled as DEEE under the AGEC law, with traceable recycling documents for unsold or returned memory units.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises require a fire safety certificate issued by the Prefecture's commission de sécurité, proving compliance with the fire-resistance, emergency exit, smoke detection and extinguishing provisions of the Code du travail and local safety rules. A structural load certificate for the mezzanine or racking is required if the storage area exceeds ordinary building supervisor thresholds, and an occupational risk assessment covering electrical installations, employee access, ergonomic handling and first aid equipment must be completed and kept available.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — official portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate and VAT filing via pro.impots.gouv.fr; business registration interfaced through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-incorporated SAS, the one-stop business formality acquires the SIREN, SIRET and intra-community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) automatically from DGFiP upon incorporation; no separate tax election is required. For a non-resident entity without a French establishment, the non-established taxable person must file Form 3318-CA (CA3/3318-CA) with the DGFiP Non-Résidents unit to obtain a direct French VAT number; if the entity is established outside the EU, an accredited fiscal representative must be appointed before registration; registration must precede the first taxable supply in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is mandatorily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level; no pass-through check-the-box election exists in France. Available elections: intra-group fiscal integration under CGI Art. 223A for 95%-owned French subsidiaries; option for the reduced corporate tax rate for SMEs (15% on first €42,500 profit); election to carry back tax losses (créance de carry-back) under set conditions; hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD/EU Directive 2016/1164 are mandatory and cannot be opted out; DAC6/hallmark reporting obligations apply to cross-border arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for wholesale B2B supplies; VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply in France. The domestic small-business exemption (franchise en base) applies only to established SMEs with turnover below €85,000 for goods and €37,500 for services, and does not apply to non-established entities, large enterprises, or the wholesale brokerage of semiconductors.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for all domestic B2B transactions is being phased in from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs and other businesses. Invoice data and transaction data must be transmitted to the DGFiP through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or certified private platforms (PDPs) using structured electronic formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII). Electronic reporting (e-reporting) of cross-border supplies is mandatory. The French model is a continuous clearance and data-reporting obligation, not a real-time fiscal stamping or receipt-authorisation regime; penalties for non-compliance escalate up to €15,000 per violation and are capped at €1 million.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union are zero-rated under CGI Arts. 262(I)(1) and 258 when ownership risk transfer occurs and the exporter obtains and preserves proof that the goods physically departed from the EU territory within the statutory period. Supplies of services ancillary to exported goods (brokerage, commission, logistics) qualify for zero-rating when supplied to a non-EU recipient or when directly linked to exported goods. Export of CPU chips and SSDs to non-EU buyers meets the 0% VAT rate provided the shipping terms are sufficient proof (FOB/CIF/EXW with export evidence) and the transaction is recorded in the export declaration. Intra-EU dispatches to registered EU customers are exempt under VDDI rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation in DELTA/DÉMONIQUE)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR or other transport document evidencing transfer of goods at EU exit
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Export contract or purchase order showing ownership transfer
Intra-Community sales list (EC Sales List) or French export declaration summary for EU VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and French Customs perform targeted e-audits of zero-rated exporters using transaction data from DELTA, the export declaration system, and FATCA/CRS exchange data. A fraudulent export zero-rating claim is treated as tax fraud (fraude fiscale) under CGI Art. 1741, subject to a retrospective VAT reassessment within 3 years (extended to 6 years in concealment/fraud cases), plus interest at the statutory rate (4% quarterly), issue of a 40% or 80% penalty (insuffisance de déclaration / manoeuvres frauduleuses), and criminal fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Customs may independently impose penalties under French Customs Code Arts. 414-2 and 423 for falsified export documents. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day foreign-exchange settlement deadline also triggers transfer-pricing documentation scrutiny and may invalidate the economic substance of the export claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) and the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) under the aegis of the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy; foreign exchange administration is delegated to the Ministry of Economy and Finance via the Direction Générale du Trésor (DGT) and the Banque de France for reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under full capital and current account convertibility as a member of the Eurozone and OECD. The euro is freely convertible; no exchange controls exist for current account transactions (trade, services, remittances) or capital account operations (direct investment, loans, portfolio flows). Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to standard corporate tax withholding (if applicable under treaty) and anti-money laundering (AML) verification. No prior authorization is required for cross-border transfers exceeding €10,000, but they must be reported to the customs authorities for statistical purposes. The only restrictions apply to transactions with sanctioned countries (e.g., Russia, Iran) or dual-use goods, which require specific licenses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds into euros. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts (comptes devises) with authorized banks. However, all export receipts exceeding €12,500 must be declared to the Banque de France via the 'Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds' (DTF) within 30 days of the transaction. For trade in semiconductor goods (ISIC 4651), the exporter must also comply with EU dual-use export control regulations (Regulation (EU) 2021/821) if the goods are classified as dual-use (e.g., high-performance processors). No conversion ratio applies; the exporter may freely choose to convert or hold foreign currency.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. French fintech EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Manager.one) are licensed as Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the ACPR and can provide multi-currency accounts, SWIFT transfers, and FX services. However, they are generally not suitable for capital escrow accounts or high-volume trade finance due to lower transaction limits, limited credit facilities, and less robust correspondent banking networks. For cross-border semiconductor trading, a tier-1 bank is recommended for settlement and LC operations. EMIs may be used for operational expenses and smaller disbursements, but they face restrictions on accepting cash and may have higher compliance friction for high-risk jurisdictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity, especially for a newly formed SAS. The legal representative (Président) or a designated signatory with power of attorney must appear in person at the bank branch or via a notarized video conference (remote onboarding is permitted under French law since 2020, but most tier-1 banks still require a physical meeting for high-risk sectors). For non-resident directors, a physical visit to France is often mandatory unless the bank has a 'remote KYC' process with biometric verification and apostilled documents. The KYC interview will cover the business model, source of funds, and expected transaction volumes. For semiconductor trading, the bank will scrutinize the supply chain and end-use to ensure no dual-use violations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction counterparties (e.g., Russia, Iran, or countries on FATF grey list) in the trade chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full corporate registry extracts (Kbis) of all counterparties, beneficial ownership declarations, and a detailed explanation of the commercial rationale. Include export licenses (if any) and end-user certificates for dual-use goods. Maintain a robust transaction monitoring system and a compliance manual demonstrating enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns: rapid turnover, large wire transfers to tax havens, or inconsistent invoice values
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a comprehensive business plan with projected volumes, supplier and customer contracts, and proforma invoices. Provide audited financial statements (if available) and a clear explanation of the trade cycle. Implement a documented internal control framework and appoint a compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient proof of source of funds for capital injection (e.g., shareholder loans or equity)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide bank statements of the contributing shareholder, tax returns, and a notarized declaration of the source of wealth. For non-resident shareholders, include a legal opinion from their home jurisdiction and evidence of the corporate chain. Ensure the capital is transferred via a regulated financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use goods classification (e.g., high-performance CPUs or SSDs with encryption capabilities)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain a formal classification from the French Ministry of Economy (Direction Générale des Entreprises) confirming the goods are not dual-use or that an export license is not required. Provide technical specifications and end-user certificates. Maintain a compliance register for all transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections (equity or shareholder loans) must be routed via SWIFT wire transfer using the appropriate purpose code. For equity contributions, use purpose code 'S301' (Direct investment in France) or 'S302' (Real estate investment) as per Banque de France classification. For shareholder loans, use 'S303' (Loans between affiliated enterprises). The transfer must be accompanied by a 'Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds' (DTF) filed with the Banque de France within 30 days if the amount exceeds €12,500. The bank will require a copy of the shareholders' resolution, the SAS's Kbis, and proof of identity of the sender. For non-EU transfers, the bank may request a certificate of residence and a tax identification number. The funds must be credited to a designated capital escrow account or operational account, and the bank will verify the source of funds to comply with AML regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements (purchase of SSD/CPU chips from suppliers), the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for direct payments and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for documentary transactions. For MT103, the payment must include the correct purpose code (e.g., 'S101' for trade in goods) and the invoice reference. For LCs, the bank will issue an irrevocable LC (MT700) on behalf of the SAS, with the supplier's bank as the advising bank. The LC must be confirmed by a prime bank if the supplier is in a high-risk jurisdiction. For high-value transactions, the bank may require a pre-shipment inspection certificate and a bill of lading. The SAS should also consider using the SWIFT gpi (Global Payments Innovation) for faster tracking. For intra-EU payments, SEPA (SEPA Credit Transfer) is sufficient, but for non-EU suppliers, SWIFT is mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (maturity up to 12 months) for EUR/USD and EUR/CNY to hedge trade payables and receivables
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., INR, KRW) if the underlying trade is in those currencies
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for long-term financing or capital injections in foreign currency
FX Options (European style) for flexible hedging of contingent trade flows

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS); 3.3% social surcharge on tax exceeding EUR 763,000 yields a 25.83% top effective rate (CGI Art. 219, Art. 235 ter ZC)
